summary: 1932 Aermotor lookout on the Ochoco NF in Harney County, Oregon, preceded by a 1929 tree platform; NHLR-registered 2002, used for emergencies, listed for decommission in 2017.

facts.status_note: Standing; the Forest Service listed it for decommission as of 2017, and the tower and ground cabin are described as available for emergencies

access.note: Pages describe emergency use; the directory lists the site as legally accessible but unmanned; no source says the lookout itself is open to the public

visit.trail_note: About 12 miles of gravel from the junction of NF-41 and NF-4120; the last 4 miles are rough (trip report). Check with the managing agency before going.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two 1931 newspaper items say the steel tower was received in March 1931 and might be raised by May 1931. The Register and most other pages give 1932. The story uses 1932 and reports the 1931 items. The raising date is not confirmed by any source read.
The Register and firelookout.com give 70 feet (21.3 m). A 1931 newspaper item gives 75 feet for the tower as received and another gives 73 feet to the observation floor. The facts use 70 feet.

The Register names the U.S. Forest Service. firelookout.com lists the Ochoco National Forest with the BLM. Cheryl Hill's page says the Malheur National Forest administers the site. The facts use the Register's wording.

The Register says the lookout is still staffed, but the same description says extreme-weather staffing by the BLM began in 2000. Later pages describe emergency use, a 2017 decommission listing, and (in the July 2026 directory) an unmanned site. The facts use the later description.

notes_for_editor: Six page reads and one search. The Register, firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill and The Roaming Civic agree on the 1932 build date and the 70-foot height. Forest Lookouts quotes 1929-1934 newspaper items, which are the only source for the 1929 tree platform and the 1931 delivery. Elevation differs: the Register gives 6,241 ft (1,902 m), firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill give 6,281 ft, and the brief's 1902.3 m is the Register figure; not in facts. The Forest Lookouts history gives no fire names. The Facebook post from the Forest Fire Lookout Association could not be read (login wall), so nothing is cited from it. Access level is restricted because the sources describe emergency use and a decommission listing without an open-to-public statement. Current status: the Cheryl Hill directory (July 2026) lists it as unmanned and warns its information may be out of date; the Roaming Civic trip report is undated but post-2017. No photos added. The firelookout.com page credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum and Rex Kamstra, but no image URLs were extracted.
